# Build a real-time todo app


A full-stack reactive todo app over a single browser-to-engine WebSocket. Function calls and live
change notifications flow over the same connection. The app follows the stored records pattern from
[Recipe 2: stored records with live updates](../upgrading/migrate-from-streams#recipe-2-stored-records-with-live-updates):
the todo worker owns the data, serves queries, and announces each change through a trigger type it
owns.

## Engine configuration

The workers needed to support a browser-driven reactive app: `state` for storage and an RBAC
listener (`rbac-proxy` or `iii-worker-manager`) for browser connections. No streaming worker is
required.

## Backend

The worker, auth, storage, change trigger, and CRUD functions that power the app server-side.

### Worker setup

Connect a worker, register the functions the app needs, and bind triggers.

### Auth function (RBAC)

An auth function runs on each new browser WebSocket connection, issues a session ID, and namespaces
the session's registered functions to prevent collisions. It also limits the trigger types the
session may bind to the todo change trigger.

### Storage

Todos live in the `state` worker under one scope, one key per todo, each with a revision number that
every write increments.

### Change trigger

The todo worker declares a `todos::changed` trigger type, keeps a capped table of its bindings, and
after every committed write delivers `{ id, revision, op }` to each binding in the binding's
namespace.

### Functions

The CRUD functions the browser calls (create, toggle, delete) write to storage and then fire
`todos::changed`. `todos::get` and a paginated `todos::list` serve reads.

## Frontend

The browser-side WebSocket connection and reactive hook that render live updates.

### Connection

Connect the browser to the engine over a single WebSocket using `iii-browser-sdk`.

### Real-time hook

A hook that binds a browser function to `todos::changed`, then loads the list with `todos::list`.
Each notification re-reads one todo unless the hook already has that revision, and the hook reloads
the list after a reconnect.

## Key concepts

The reactive primitives this app relies on: single-WebSocket transport, per-session RBAC
namespacing, a worker-owned trigger type for change notifications, and a query for the initial
state and recovery.
